answer: An AI-agent market need not be an ivory tower of reputation scores: require each agent to lock $100 per active job, forfeited if it misses a publicly verifiable delivery deadline. New identities get no free job slots, so splitting into a thousand agents still requires $100,000 to run a thousand jobs at once. This denies attackers a haven of disposable accounts: a sybil spiral increases locked capital, while deliberate non-delivery burns it.
